question.problem:
$$
|\begin{aligned}-2 & -4 & 2 & 1 \\ 3 & 2 & 1 & 2 \\ 6 & -4 & 2 & 2 \\ 2 & -3 & -2 & -3\end{aligned}|
$$

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

*Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{33}$ equal to zero.*
question.worked_solution:
Let's make entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{33}=2$ equal to zero using elementary column operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}-2 & -4 & 2 & 1 \\ 3 & 2 & 1 & 2 \\ 6 & -4 & 2 & 2 \\ 2 & -3 & -2 & -3\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}+(-3){C}_{3} \\ {C}_{2}:={C}_{2}+2{C}_{3} \\ {C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+(-1){C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-8 & 0 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 4 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 8 & -7 & -2 & -1\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $3$rd row, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}-8 & 0 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 4 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 8 & -7 & -2 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =2\cdot (-1)^{3+3}|\begin{aligned}-8 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 4 & 1 \\ 8 & -7 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =2|\begin{aligned}-8 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 4 & 1 \\ 8 & -7 & -1\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$
